_meta.purpose: The only stack list on the site. The résumé, the /skills/ page and the About page all render from here, which is why the old site's three disagreeing lists cannot recur.
_meta.noPercentages: Deliberately no percentages and no bars. A '90% Playwright' bar encodes nothing a reader can check. Three levels with a definition each, and every Core claim linking to the work that proves it, encodes something.
_meta.jsonLd: `knowsAbout` in the Person JSON-LD is emitted from entries with level 'core' only.

core.label: Core
core.definition: I have built and owned production systems with this, made design decisions I can defend, and hit its limits. Every Core entry links to the work.

working.label: Working
working.definition: I use this regularly and productively. I would not claim to know its edges.

familiar.label: Familiar
familiar.definition: I have shipped something with it, or maintain code that uses it. I would need a ramp-up before owning it.

groups.name: AI evaluation and quality
groups.lede: The centre of what I do. Deciding whether a generated answer is good enough to send to a person asking about their pregnancy.

skills.name: LLM-as-a-judge design
skills.note: Judge independence, binary verdicts over floating scores, calibration against human annotation.

skills.name: Golden dataset design
skills.note: Multilingual, stratified, versioned in git alongside the code it gates.

skills.name: RAGAS
skills.note: Faithfulness and context precision as nightly CI signals, not a report nobody opens.

skills.name: Production evaluation pipelines
skills.note: Anomaly-triggered sampling on live traffic, human annotation loop, alerting.

skills.name: Semantic cache correctness validation
skills.note: Precision and recall gated at different thresholds, because a false hit and a miss are not the same failure.

skills.name: RAG retrieval evaluation
skills.note: One of the six programs I cover is RAG. I evaluate it; I did not build the retrieval architecture.

groups.name: Test automation
groups.lede: Four and a half years of it, including the part where I retired two frameworks I had built.

skills.name: Playwright
skills.note: 300+ scenarios, native sharding across six runners, visual regression.

skills.name: Contract testing with Pact
skills.note: Provider states, broker, can-i-deploy as a real deployment gate.

skills.name: API test design
skills.note: 30+ endpoints across five backend services.

skills.name: Visual regression
skills.note: Tight pixel tolerance, CI-only baselines. Cross-OS font rendering makes local baselines a trap.

skills.name: Robot Framework and pabot
skills.note: Two years of it, then the diagnosis that four of its limits were structural.

skills.name: Botium
skills.note: 140+ conversational flows. Maintained as an internal fork; upstream adoption collapsed after the 2022 acquisition.

skills.name: Service virtualization and mock design

groups.name: Infrastructure and pipelines
groups.lede: Enough to own the systems my tests run on, and to be useful in a design review about them.

skills.name: Docker
skills.note: Containerising the test environment eliminated a class of CI breakage caused by Chrome and driver versions drifting apart.

skills.name: AWS (Lambda, MSK, EC2, SQS, Parameter Store)

groups.name: Data and analytics
groups.lede: The data platform function came with the sole-QA role. Most of the quality problems I find now are data problems.

skills.name: SQL
skills.note: Window functions, CTEs, geospatial predicates. Test design, not just reporting.

skills.name: Production traffic analysis
skills.note: Reading what users actually send, rather than what the test set assumes they send.

skills.name: OWASP ZAP

skills.name: Quality strategy ownership
skills.note: Sole QA across six country programs and six-plus AI product lines.

skills.name: Framework retirement discipline
skills.note: The hard half of framework work. Retiring one I built, with a full parallel-run cycle proving zero divergence before decommissioning.

skills.name: Scrum Master

skills.name: Mentoring
skills.note: One senior engineer with no automation background and two campus recruits through a four-month programme.
